title: Emptying ashtrays and smoking urns without a fire risk
audience: Cleaners who empty and clean ashtrays and smoking urns at building entrances and outdoor areas.
learningOutcomes: Explain why an ashtray must be treated as hot until it has been checked.
Empty a sand-filled or non-sand ashtray using the correct method and protective equipment.
Replace ashtray filler when scooping no longer clears it.

instruction.heading: Heat is the first hazard
instruction.body: Smoking urns and ashtrays often hold embers that look out but are still burning inside. Treat every ashtray as hot until you have checked it. Embers never go into a plastic liner or any general waste bin, because the bag can melt or start a fire. If you are unsure how to handle a particular urn, ask the site contact for their method before you touch it.

instruction.heading: Sand-filled urns
instruction.body: Wear eye protection and gloves. Lift cigarette ends and debris out of the sand with a scoop, making several passes so the sand is clear. Put the debris into a sealed plastic bag once it has cooled, and close the bag so the smell stays inside. Some sites use cat litter as the filler. The same method applies. Replace the filler when scooping no longer clears it: empty the old material into a sealed bag, wipe the base and rim with a damp cloth, then refill to just below the rim and level the surface.

instruction.heading: Non-sand ashtrays
instruction.body: Remove the ashtray where possible and empty it into a sealed bag once the contents are cool. If it cannot be removed, scoop the debris out. Wipe clean with a damp cloth, use soapy water for stubborn stains, and dry the ashtray before it goes back into use.

procedure: Check the ashtray for embers and treat it as hot until it has been checked.
Put on eye protection and gloves.
Sand-filled: scoop debris into a sealed bag in several passes until the sand is clear.
Replace the filler when scooping no longer clears it, and wipe the base and rim.
Non-sand: remove the ashtray if possible, empty it into a sealed bag, wipe and dry.
Return the urn or ashtray to use only when it is clear, dry and level.

workedExamples.situation: The sand in an urn is grey and smells strongly after one scoop, and butts are still visible.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: Should you scoop again, or replace the filler?
workedExamples.reasoning: If repeated scooping does not clear the sand, replace the filler. Empty the old material into a sealed bag once cool, clean the base and rim, and refill to the correct level before the urn goes back into use.

equipmentAndPpe: Filler material (sand or cat litter, as the site uses)

commonErrors.error: Tipping hot ash into a plastic bag.
commonErrors.prevention: Treat all ash as hot until checked, and wait for it to cool before bagging.

commonErrors.error: Filling the urn above the rim.
commonErrors.prevention: Stop just below the rim and level the surface.

commonErrors.error: Skipping gloves because the job looks quick.
commonErrors.prevention: Put on gloves and glasses before opening the urn.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Embers can stay hot after the top looks grey. Treat ash as hot until you have checked it.
Know where the nearest fire extinguisher is and what the site's fire procedure says before handling ash.
Specific fire-safety duties and waste-handling rules vary by state or territory, so check with the relevant regulator before relying on this point.

qualityStandard: The urn is free of butts and debris.
The filler is level and sits below the rim.
The ashtray base is dry before it returns to use.
documentationEvidence: Filler replacements recorded with the date.
summary: Treat every ashtray as hot until checked, and never bag embers with general waste.
Scoop in several passes; replace the filler when scooping no longer clears it.
Wear eye protection and gloves, and know the site's fire procedure.

knowledgeChecks.question: Why must embers never go into a plastic bag with general waste?
options: Because the bag can melt or start a fire
Because the bag would be too light to lift
Because the bag would make the smell worse

knowledgeChecks.question: After several scoops, the filler still shows butts and smells. What is the right action?
options: Add perfume to hide the smell and leave the old filler in place
Replace the filler after emptying the old material into a sealed bag
Scoop harder and change nothing else and keep scooping for the rest of the day

knowledgeChecks.question: What must be worn for this task?
options: A dust mask and a hat

knowledgeChecks.question: How does the lesson say every ashtray must be treated?
options: As cold, since it looks empty
As clean, if the sand is smooth
As hot until it has been checked
